lead.headline: 11% of San Antonio hospice ID numbers sit in "farms": one signer, 4+ hospice names, one address. Elsewhere: 0.5%
lead.number: 31 of 282 active San Antonio hospice IDs (11.0%) vs 0.53% outside California, Houston and San Antonio; Houston 4-7%, California 3.3%; Houston's Suite 610 five trace to two signers, in a building holding 14 hospice IDs since 2008
lead.watch_out: No hospice payment data exists in the warehouse, so nothing shows any of these IDs billed Medicare a dollar; and the signer isn't necessarily the owner.

sources.quote: Of the newest entrants, 308 were co-located with at least one other hospice at the same address, and 15 separate hospice agencies were found operating out of a single building on Loop 410 in San Antonio.
McNair's research found as many as 15 hospices operating out of a single building, all under the same owner.
Take 10 patients, multiply that times 15 hospices working under one building, under one owner, and you can do the math.
In November, ProPublica and The New Yorker highlighted that the four states were overrun with for-profit hospices, many of them sharing the same addresses and owners.

It found dozens of hospice agencies were often clustered in the same building as well as a rapid increase in the number of hospices being established and abnormally high rates of patients being discharged.
